{"records":[{"id":"S01","section":"SUMMARY","text":"The principal dispute concerns O. P. Kathpalia's tenancy and continued possession of the cottage attached to the bungalow at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi. E. B. Brook originally leased the bungalow and inducted Kathpalia as a subtenant of the cottage. After Brook surrendered his tenancy, the original landlord, Lakhmir Singh, accepted Kathpalia as his direct tenant effective May 1, 1955. Lakhmir Singh subsequently transferred the entire property to respondents Nos. 2 and 3, who became the real contesting respondents. The litigation concerned the timeliness and determination of standard rent, the landlord's claim for arrears and possession, the validity of an alleged future-rent deposit direction, and the tenant's right to defend the possession suit.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_RECOUNTED_FACT_AND_PROCEDURAL_HISTORY","stage":"Overall tenancy, standard-rent and possession litigation","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A03","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E03","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E04","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E07"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L53","IK-1954254:L54","IK-1954254:L56","IK-1954254:L59","IK-1954254:L169"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"HEAD_TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04"},{"role":"TRANSFEREE","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A03"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S02","section":"GROUND","text":"Brook inducted Kathpalia as a subtenant of the cottage on September 1, 1954, after commencement of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952. Brook surrendered his head tenancy on April 1, 1955, but Kathpalia remained in possession. By an agreement reached in June 1955, Lakhmir Singh accepted Kathpalia as a direct tenant effective May 1, 1955. The Supreme Court treated this subsequent direct tenancy as the relevant letting for the limitation dispute.","status":"ADMITTED_POSITION_RECOGNIZED_BY_SUPREME_COURT","stage":"Tenancy formation and classification for Section 11(b)","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L53","IK-1954254:L54","IK-1954254:L90","IK-1954254:L91","IK-1954254:L99","IK-1954254:L100"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"HEAD_TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S03","section":"GROUND","text":"Under Section 11(b), as construed and adopted by the Supreme Court, the six-month period for a standard-rent application concerning premises let after commencement of the Act runs from the commencement of the relevant letting to the particular applicant tenant. It does not necessarily run from the first-ever letting of the premises or from an earlier subtenancy that preceded recognition of the applicant's direct tenancy. The Court reasoned that the contrary construction would prevent subsequent tenants from challenging unreasonable rent and frustrate the protective purpose of the legislation.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_LEGAL_INTERPRETATION","stage":"Supreme Court review of Section 11(b) limitation","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E06"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L83","IK-1954254:L86","IK-1954254:L101","IK-1954254:L102","IK-1954254:L103","IK-1954254:L104","IK-1954254:L106","IK-1954254:L107"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S04","section":"GROUND","text":"The Supreme Court distinguished Kathpalia's earlier post-Act subtenancy from his subsequently recognized direct tenancy. It observed that the record contained no evidence establishing that Lakhmir Singh had given written consent to Brook's induction of Kathpalia as subtenant. In discussing Sections 2(j) and 13(1)(b), the Court explained the statutory significance of unauthorized post-Act subletting, but did not finally adjudicate a separate eviction claim based on unlawful subletting. The absence of evidence of written consent is an evidentiary assessment, not independent proof that consent could never have existed.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_INTERPRETIVE_REASONING_AND_EVIDENTIARY_ASSESSMENT","stage":"Classification of post-Act subtenancy and direct tenancy","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L97","IK-1954254:L98","IK-1954254:L99","IK-1954254:L100"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"HEAD_TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S05","section":"GROUND","text":"Kathpalia filed his Section 8 application for determination of standard rent in October 1955. The judgment records October 10, 1955 in its factual chronology but also reproduces October 1, 1955 when describing the trial court's reasoning. Both stated dates fall within six calendar months of the direct tenancy's effective commencement on May 1, 1955. The Supreme Court expressly held that the application was within time. This statement reports the Court's adopted conclusion; the conflicting filing-date references are not resolved into a single verified date.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_LIMITATION_HOLDING_WITH_SOURCE_DATE_DISCREPANCY","stage":"Section 8 application and Supreme Court limitation review","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A05","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E03","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E06"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L54","IK-1954254:L55","IK-1954254:L92","IK-1954254:L93","IK-1954254:L106","IK-1954254:L109"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S06","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"The District Judge rejected Kathpalia's standard-rent application as time-barred by treating his September 1, 1954 induction as Brook's subtenant, or the earlier letting of the premises, as controlling the limitation period despite his subsequent direct tenancy effective May 1, 1955. The Punjab High Court substantially adopted that interpretation. The Supreme Court expressly rejected their construction of Section 11(b), holding that limitation must be assessed by reference to the relevant letting to the applicant tenant. The lower-court construction is reported solely as a rejected contrary position and is not an operative legal premise.","status":"REPORTED_LOWER_COURT_REASONING_EXPRESSLY_REJECTED_BY_SUPREME_COURT","stage":"District Judge appeal, High Court revision and Supreme Court limitation review","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A06","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A07","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E04","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E06"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L57","IK-1954254:L58","IK-1954254:L94","IK-1954254:L95","IK-1954254:L101","IK-1954254:L102","IK-1954254:L103","IK-1954254:L104","IK-1954254:L108","IK-1954254:L109"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"HEAD_TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A04"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A06"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S07","section":"GROUND","text":"On August 4, 1960, the trial court held Kathpalia's standard-rent application timely and fixed standard rent at Rs. 855 per annum. The District Judge allowed the landlord-side appeal on limitation grounds without deciding the proper amount, and the High Court upheld that limitation approach. Because the amount had not been examined by those appellate courts, the Supreme Court allowed Civil Appeal No. 464 of 1971, set aside the adverse limitation decisions, and remitted the landlord's appeal to the District Judge for determination of the proper standard rent. The Supreme Court did not finally fix or affirm Rs. 855 per annum as the operative standard rent.","status":"TRIAL_COURT_FINDING_AND_SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_REMAND_DISPOSITION","stage":"Standard-rent determination, Civil Appeal No. 464 of 1971","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A03","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A05","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A06","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A07","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E03","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E04","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E06"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L56","IK-1954254:L57","IK-1954254:L58","IK-1954254:L109","IK-1954254:L110","IK-1954254:L111","IK-1954254:L171"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"TRANSFEREE","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A03"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S08","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"Lakhmir Singh commenced Civil Suit No. 231/56 on July 3, 1956, seeking recovery of rent arrears and possession under Section 13(1)(a), alleging default despite a demand notice dated May 10, 1956. Kathpalia disputed the claim, explaining that his standard-rent application was pending and that the claimed arrears were calculated at the disputed contractual rate. The landlord's pleaded nonpayment allegation is not equivalent to a judicial determination that every statutory condition for eviction was satisfied.","status":"LANDLORD_CLAIM_REPORTED_AND_TENANT_DEFENCE_REPORTED_NOT_FINAL_MERITS_FINDING","stage":"Trial court rent recovery and possession suit","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A05"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L59","IK-1954254:L60","IK-1954254:L61","IK-1954254:L114"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S09","section":"GROUND","text":"Kathpalia deposited the arrears of rent claimed by Lakhmir Singh during the trial proceedings, under protest and while maintaining his challenge to the contractual rate. The Supreme Court noted that the claimed arrears had been deposited at the first hearing. This is an actual historical deposit of previously claimed arrears; it does not establish payment of subsequently accruing future rent, compliance with any later valid interim-rent determination, or satisfaction of the separate one-month statutory payment-or-tender condition following a qualifying demand notice.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_RECOUNTED_ACTUAL_DEPOSIT_WITH_LIMITED_LEGAL_EFFECT","stage":"Eviction suit and Section 13(1)(a) payment dispute","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A05","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E01"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L61","IK-1954254:L62","IK-1954254:L72","IK-1954254:L114","IK-1954254:L134"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S10","section":"GROUND","text":"Lakhmir Singh applied on August 1, 1956 for permission to withdraw the arrears deposited by Kathpalia and separately applied on August 27, 1956 under Section 13(5) for directions requiring future rent to be deposited month by month. Kathpalia opposed withdrawal before standard rent had been determined and sought interim-rent determination under Section 9 on October 5, 1956. These applications were procedural requests by the respective parties. Filing them did not itself establish an effective future-rent deposit order or actual payment under such an order.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_RECOUNTED_PROCEDURAL_HISTORY","stage":"Trial suit rent applications and Section 9 interim-rent request","actor_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A05"],"property_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/P01"],"event_ids":["1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E01","1954254/633f2f3edf116962/E02"],"refs":["IK-1954254:L61","IK-1954254:L62","IK-1954254:L63","IK-1954254:L114","IK-1954254:L115","IK-1954254:L116","IK-1954254:L118"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A02"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A01"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1954254/633f2f3edf116962/A08"}]},{"id":"S11","section":"GROUND","text":"The Supreme Court adopted the statutory reasoning that Section 13 protects a tenant against recovery of possession unless an applicable statutory enabling ground is established. Mr. Brook surrendered his tenancy and vacated the portion in his actual possession on April 1, 1955 simultaneously calling upon the appellant to hand over possession of premises in his possession to the then landlord one Lakhmir Singh, who is no more.

Appellant did not vacate the premises in his possession but reached an agreement with Lakhmir Singh, the then landlord on June 20/22, 1955 to become the direct tenant of the then landlord of the premises in his possession on a monthly rent of Rs. 277.50 p. as stated in plaint, effective from May 1,1955.

Landlord Lakhmir Singh entered appearance and contested the application inter-alia contending that the petition was barred by limitation.
IK-1954254:L56
The trial court held that the petition was not barred by limitation and fixed the standard rent at Rs. 855/- p.a. with effect from October 1, 1955. This decision was rendered on Aug. 4, 1960.In the meantime, landlord Lakhmir Singh sold the whole bungalow including the demised premises by a deed of conveyance dated December 21, 1959 in favour of respondents Nos. 2 and 3 who on their own were impleaded in the proceedings.

The original landlord Lakhmir Singh and the two transferees from Lakhmir Singh preferred an appeal against the order of the learned Single Judge determining the standard rent: in the court of the District Judge, Delhi. Accordingly the appeal was allowed and the petition of the appellant was dismissed.
IK-1954254:L58

A learned Judge of the High Court agreed with the view taken by the learned District Judge that the petition was barred by limitation and accordingly rejected the civil revision petition by his judgment and order dated December 17, 1962 against which the appellant has preferred Civil Appeal No. 464 of 1971 by special leave.
IK-1954254:L59

During the pendency of the proceedings for determination of standard rent in the trial court, the then landlord Likhmir Singh filed Civil Suit No. 231/56 in the Court of the Senior Sub Judge, at Delhi on July 3, 1956 against the appellant for recovering the arrears of rent and possession.
